description: The LITERARY world: authors, forms, and the canon of allusions — a timeless / universal-region anchor. Holds the agent's own name (Jabberwock, from Carroll).

microtheory.name: literature
microtheory.definition: Literature: poems, novels, verse and prose, and the canon of allusions that graduate from a source into common usage. A timeless world present in every manifold — Cornelius Vane the Victorian holds it as fully as a modern gamer.

concepts.name: carroll
concepts.definition: Lewis Carroll (Charles Dodgson, 1832-1898), author of Alice and the Jabberwock.

concepts.name: dickens
concepts.definition: Charles Dickens (1812-1870), the pre-eminent Victorian novelist.

concepts.name: shakespeare
concepts.definition: William Shakespeare, the canonical English dramatist and poet.

concepts.name: melville
concepts.definition: Herman Melville (1819-1891), author of Moby-Dick — 'call me Ishmael'.

concepts.name: alice
concepts.definition: Alice, the child protagonist of Carroll's Wonderland and Looking-Glass.

concepts.name: jabberwock
concepts.definition: Carroll's nonsense monster, coined in the poem 'Jabberwocky' (1871). The agent is named after it — the deepest literary allusion it carries.

concepts.name: jabberwocky
concepts.definition: Carroll's 1871 nonsense poem, source of the Jabberwock and the word itself.

concepts.name: wonderland
concepts.definition: The dream world of Carroll's 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' (1865).

concepts.name: rabbit_hole
concepts.definition: Alice's descent in Wonderland — graduated into 'down the rabbit hole', a universal idiom for a descent into complexity or the surreal.

concepts.name: red_queen
concepts.definition: Carroll's Looking-Glass queen — graduated into 'the Red Queen', running to stay in place, a universal idiom for perpetual competition.

concepts.name: through_the_looking_glass
concepts.definition: Carroll's 1871 sequel to Wonderland, source of the Red Queen.

concepts.name: allusion
concepts.definition: A brief, indirect reference to a work, person, or event, live only where its world is.

concepts.name: poem
concepts.definition: A composition in verse, the literary form of Jabberwocky.

concepts.name: verse
concepts.definition: Metrical writing arranged in lines, the substance of a poem.

concepts.name: prose
concepts.definition: Ordinary written language without metrical structure — the form of the novel.

concepts.name: nonsense_verse
concepts.definition: Verse built from invented and playful words — the genre of Jabberwocky.

concepts.name: allusion_form
concepts.definition: The literary device of alluding — a reference whose liveness is manifold-relative.
